meta.title: ProGramerly - Basic Coding Software for All
meta.author: Johan Wilhelm van Antwerp

full.label: Full Stack
full.desc: Everything. Every app, every runtime, every SDK, every shell, comms and drives. Local AI is opt-in (tick AEDi local core). ~50-80 GB, 70-140 min.

ai.label: AI Dev
ai.desc: Claude, Gemini, Codex, Copilot, MCP servers, Firebase, Node, Python, Git, VS Code. Local models are opt-in (tick AEDi local core). ~8-14 GB.

minimal.label: Minimal
minimal.desc: Git, Node, Python, VS Code, Chrome, PowerShell. ~4-8 GB.

embedded.label: Maker & Embedded
embedded.desc: Arduino IDE 2 + cores, PlatformIO, ESP-IDF, MicroPython, serial tools, KiCad, Pi Imager, VS Code with the embedded extension set, Python, Git. ~8-14 GB.

groups.label: Package Managers
groups.desc: The engines everything else rides on - winget, Chocolatey, Homebrew, apt/dnf/pacman, Flatpak, snap.

groups.label: Source Control
groups.desc: Git, GitHub CLI, GitHub Desktop, GitKraken, lazygit - on Windows, macOS and Linux.

groups.label: Shells & Terminal
groups.desc: All shells, updated.

groups.label: Language Runtimes
groups.desc: Node (fnm + system + toolbelt), Bun, Deno, Python, .NET, Java, Go, Rust, C/C++.

groups.label: IDEs & Editors
groups.desc: Visual Studio 2026, VS Code, Kiro, Cursor, Windsurf, Zed, JetBrains, Eclipse, Sublime, Android Studio, Unity, Godot.

groups.label: Desktop Apps
groups.desc: Claude, Chrome, OBS, Canva, Obsidian, Notion, Miro, PowerToys, LibreOffice.

groups.label: Browsers & Extensions
groups.desc: Chrome, Edge, Firefox Dev, ad blocking, Claude in Chrome.

groups.label: Communication
groups.desc: WhatsApp, Teams, Zoom, Slack, Discord, Telegram, Signal. Installed, never signed in.

groups.label: Cloud Drives & Sync
groups.desc: Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, rclone. Installed - you sign in, ProGramerly never does.

groups.label: AI CLIs & Models
groups.desc: Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex CLI, Copilot CLI, Ollama, LM Studio.

groups.label: ML & AI Frameworks
groups.desc: Managed venv, PyTorch, TensorFlow, Transformers, LangChain.

groups.label: MCP Servers
groups.desc: Model Context Protocol servers Claude Desktop uses.

groups.label: Databases
groups.desc: SQLite, MongoDB, PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Redis, clients.

groups.label: Web Stacks
groups.desc: Apache + MySQL + PHP, Laravel, Rails, Django, React, Express, .NET.

groups.label: Mobile & Cross-platform
groups.desc: Flutter, Dart, Kotlin, Android SDK, React Native, Expo.

groups.label: Embedded & IoT
groups.desc: Arduino IDE 2 + cores, arduino-cli, PlatformIO, ESP-IDF, MicroPython, Thonny, serial terminals, Pi Imager.

groups.label: Maker · CAD · PCB · 3D

groups.label: APIs & Testing

groups.label: SDKs / ADKs / Cloud

groups.label: Core Libraries & Tools

items.name: winget (Windows Package Manager)
items.desc: Verifies winget is present; repairs the App Installer source if broken.

items.name: Chocolatey
items.desc: Fallback package engine for anything winget cannot resolve.

steps.cmd: if (-not (Get-Command choco -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue)) { Set-ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Scope Process -Force; [System.Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol = 3072; iex ((New-Object System.Net.WebClient).DownloadString('https://community.chocolatey.org/install.ps1')) } else { choco --version }

items.name: Homebrew
items.desc: The macOS package engine. Installed non-interactively if missing.

items.name: Xcode Command Line Tools
items.desc: Apple's compiler toolchain. Required by Homebrew and most native builds.

items.name: Linux package sources (apt/dnf/pacman + Flatpak + snap)
items.desc: Refreshes the native package index, installs Flatpak with the Flathub remote and snapd where the distro allows it. Every Linux item rides on this.

steps.cmd: sh -c 'if command -v apt-get >/dev/null; then sudo apt-get update; elif command -v dnf >/dev/null; then sudo dnf makecache; elif command -v pacman >/dev/null; then sudo pacman -Sy --noconfirm; elif command -v zypper >/dev/null; then sudo zypper refresh; fi'

sh -c 'if command -v apt-get >/dev/null; then sudo apt-get install -y flatpak curl wget ca-certificates gnupg; elif command -v dnf >/dev/null; then sudo dnf install -y flatpak curl wget; elif command -v pacman >/dev/null; then sudo pacman -S --noconfirm --needed flatpak curl wget; fi'
sh -c 'if command -v apt-get >/dev/null && ! command -v snap >/dev/null; then sudo apt-get install -y snapd; fi'

items.name: Git
items.desc: Distributed version control. On Windows this also brings Git Bash.

items.name: GitHub CLI
items.desc: gh - clone, PR, release and auth from the terminal.

items.name: GitHub Desktop
items.desc: GitHub Desktop - the graphical Git client. Windows and macOS from GitHub; Linux from the shiftkey community build (apt/rpm repo, Flatpak fallback).

pre.cmd:
sh -c 'if command -v apt-get >/dev/null; then wget -qO- https://apt.packages.shiftkey.dev/gpg.key | gpg --dearmor | sudo tee /usr/share/keyrings/shiftkey-packages.gpg >/dev/null && echo "deb [arch=amd64 signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/shiftkey-packages.gpg] https://apt.packages.shiftkey.dev/ubuntu/ any main" | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/shiftkey-packages.list >/dev/null && sudo apt-get update; elif command -v dnf >/dev/null; then sudo rpm --import https://rpm.packages.shiftkey.dev/gpg.key && printf "[shiftkey-packages]
name=GitHub Desktop
baseurl=https://rpm.packages.shiftkey.dev/rpm/
enabled=1
gpgcheck=1
repo_gpgcheck=1
gpgkey=https://rpm.packages.shiftkey.dev/gpg.key
" | sudo tee /etc/yum.repos.d/shiftkey-packages.repo >/dev/null; fi'

items.name: Git LFS
items.desc: Large file storage for binary assets.

items.name: GitKraken + lazygit
items.desc: A GUI and a TUI for the day the terminal is not enough.

items.name: PowerShell 7+
items.desc: Cross-platform PowerShell (pwsh). Sits alongside Windows PowerShell 5.1.

items.name: Windows Terminal
items.desc: Tabbed terminal host for cmd, PowerShell, WSL and Git Bash.

items.name: OpenSSH (client + agent)
items.desc: The ssh client, ssh-keygen and ssh-add, plus the ssh-agent service enabled so a passphrase-protected key is typed once per boot instead of once per push.

steps.cmd: $c = Get-WindowsCapability -Online -Name 'OpenSSH.Client*' | Where-Object { $_.State -ne 'Installed' }; if ($c) { Add-WindowsCapability -Online -Name $c.Name | Out-Null }; (Get-Command ssh -ErrorAction Stop).Source
Set-Service ssh-agent -StartupType Automatic; Start-Service ssh-agent; Write-Output "ssh-agent: $((Get-Service ssh-agent).Status)"

items.name: Nushell
items.desc: Structured-data shell. Good for pipelines that carry tables, not text.

items.name: Oh My Posh
items.desc: Prompt theme engine for every shell.

items.name: Starship prompt
items.desc: Minimal, fast, cross-shell prompt.

items.name: Update all shells & package sources
items.desc: winget source update + choco upgrade all / brew update && brew upgrade.

items.name: Node.js (LTS + Latest via fnm)
items.desc: fnm version manager, then Node LTS and Node Latest, LTS set as default.

post.cmd: eval "$(fnm env)" && fnm install --lts && fnm install latest && fnm default lts-latest

items.name: Node.js LTS (system install)
items.desc: A plain system Node so global CLIs work even before fnm is on PATH.

pre.cmd: sh -c 'if command -v apt-get >/dev/null; then curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_lts.x | sudo -E bash -; fi'

items.name: pnpm, Yarn, npm-check-updates
items.desc: The other JS package managers plus a dependency upgrader.

items.name: Node toolbelt (pm2, nodemon, vite, tsx, eslint, prettier, ncu, serve)
items.desc: The globals every Node project reaches for: process manager, watcher, bundler, TS runner, linter, formatter, dependency updater, static server.

items.name: Bun + Deno
items.desc: The two other JavaScript runtimes.

items.name: Electron + Electron Builder + Forge
items.desc: Desktop app stack (this installer is built on it).

items.name: TypeScript + tsx + ESLint + Prettier
items.desc: The standard TS toolchain, installed globally.

items.name: Python 3 (latest + 3.12)
items.desc: Latest CPython plus 3.12 for compatibility, with py launcher on Windows.

post.winCmd: py -3 -m pip install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel
post.cmd: python3 -m pip install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel
python3 -m pip install --upgrade --break-system-packages pip setuptools wheel

items.name: uv, pipx, poetry, ruff
items.desc: Modern Python packaging and lint stack.

post.cmd: py -3 -m pip install --user pipx poetry ruff

items.name: .NET SDK (all supported LTS + current)
items.desc: .NET 10, 9 and 8 SDKs side by side, plus the ASP.NET runtimes.

items.name: .NET Framework 4.8 Dev Pack
items.desc: Legacy Framework targeting pack for older Windows projects.

items.name: Java JDK (Temurin 21 LTS + 17 LTS)
items.desc: Eclipse Temurin OpenJDK builds.

items.name: Go
items.desc: The Go toolchain.

items.name: Rust (rustup)
items.desc: rustup, cargo and the stable toolchain.

items.name: C/C++ toolchain (LLVM, CMake, Ninja)
items.desc: Clang/LLVM, CMake and Ninja. MSVC comes with Visual Studio.

items.name: Ruby & PHP
items.desc: Rounds out the mainstream scripting languages.

items.name: Visual Studio Code
items.desc: The editor. Extensions are installed in a follow-up step.

pre.cmd:
sh -c 'if command -v apt-get >/dev/null; then wget -qO- https://packages.microsoft.com/keys/microsoft.asc | gpg --dearmor | sudo tee /usr/share/keyrings/microsoft.gpg >/dev/null && echo "deb [arch=amd64,arm64 signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/microsoft.gpg] https://packages.microsoft.com/repos/code stable main" | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/vscode.list >/dev/null && sudo apt-get update; elif command -v dnf >/dev/null; then sudo rpm --import https://packages.microsoft.com/keys/microsoft.asc && printf "[code]
name=Visual Studio Code
baseurl=https://packages.microsoft.com/yumrepos/vscode
enabled=1
gpgcheck=1
gpgkey=https://packages.microsoft.com/keys/microsoft.asc
" | sudo tee /etc/yum.repos.d/vscode.repo >/dev/null; fi'

items.name: Visual Studio Code Insiders
items.desc: The nightly VS Code build, installed beside stable as `code-insiders`. Same settings sync, separate extensions.

items.name: VS Code extension pack (critical set)
items.desc: Every language server, debugger, database client, cloud tool and AI assistant a mixed stack needs - 57 extensions, installed with --force so a re-run repairs a broken one.

items.name: Visual Studio Community 2026
items.desc: The full Microsoft IDE, current release. Workloads: .NET desktop, ASP.NET & web, C++ desktop, Node.js, Azure, .NET MAUI, Python, Unity game dev, plus the recommended components. Large download (~15-30 GB). Falls back to the 2022 package if the 2026 manifest is not reachable.

items.name: Visual Studio Community 2022 (side by side)
items.desc: The previous major release, for solutions and extensions that still pin 2022. Installs beside 2026 with the same workload set. Pick this only if you need it - it is another ~15-25 GB.

items.name: Visual Studio Build Tools
items.desc: MSVC compiler, Windows SDK and CMake without the full IDE. Needed by node-gyp, native npm modules, Rust MSVC targets and PlatformIO on Windows. 2022 Build Tools are what node-gyp expects; the 2026 package is tried first and 2022 is kept as the fallback.

items.name: Android Studio + Android SDK
items.desc: Android IDE, SDK, platform tools and emulator.

items.name: Claude Desktop
items.desc: Anthropic's desktop client. MCP servers configure into this.

items.name: Google Chrome
items.desc: Browser. Also the host for the Claude in Chrome extension.

steps.cmd: sh -c 'if command -v apt-get >/dev/null; then wget -qO /tmp/chrome.deb https://dl.google.com/linux/direct/google-chrome-stable_current_amd64.deb && sudo apt-get install -y /tmp/chrome.deb; elif command -v dnf >/dev/null; then sudo dnf install -y https://dl.google.com/linux/direct/google-chrome-stable_current_x86_64.rpm; else exit 3; fi'

items.name: OBS Studio
items.desc: Screen recording and streaming.

items.name: Canva
items.desc: Design app.

items.name: Obsidian
items.desc: Local-first markdown knowledge base.

items.name: Notion
items.desc: Workspace and docs.

items.name: Miro (MIRA)
items.desc: Collaborative whiteboard desktop client.

items.name: Docker Desktop
items.desc: Containers. Several MCP servers ship as container images.

items.name: 7-Zip / Keka
items.desc: Archive tool.

items.name: Microsoft PowerToys
items.desc: FancyZones, PowerRename, Run, Color Picker, Always on Top.

items.name: LibreOffice
items.desc: Writer, Calc, Impress - and the headless converter the document pipeline uses (docx -> pdf).

items.name: Claude Code CLI
items.desc: Anthropic's agentic coding CLI. Pair it with 'Claude Code ⇄ GitHub relations' for the repo workflow.

items.name: Qwen Code CLI
items.desc: Alibaba's open-source terminal coding agent (Qwen3-Coder).

items.name: Gemini CLI
items.desc: Google's terminal agent (@google/gemini-cli). Sign in later with `gemini` - nothing is linked by ProGramerly.

items.name: OpenAI Codex CLI
items.desc: OpenAI's terminal agent. winget build on Windows, npm everywhere.

items.name: Kiro CLI (kiro-cli)
items.desc: Amazon's terminal agent, installed with Kiro's own script: Windows `irm https://cli.kiro.dev/install.ps1 | iex`, macOS/Linux `curl -fsSL https://cli.kiro.dev/install | bash`. Binary is `kiro-cli`; run `kiro-cli` once to sign in, `kiro-cli doctor` to check it.

steps.cmd: $p = @("$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\kiro-cli\kiro-cli.exe", "$env:USERPROFILE\.kiro\bin\kiro-cli.exe", "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\kiro-cli\kiro-cli.exe") | Where-Object { Test-Path $_ } | Select-Object -First 1; if ($p) { & $p --version } else { kiro-cli --version }

items.name: GitHub Copilot CLI
items.desc: GitHub Copilot in the terminal (@github/copilot). Sign in later with `copilot` - never by ProGramerly.

items.name: Claude Code ⇄ GitHub relations
items.desc: Everything Claude Code needs to work a GitHub repo: git, gh, the official claude-code-action workflow template cloned into the dev root, and a version check of each. No token, no login.

items.name: Ollama
items.desc: Run open models locally. Qwen, Llama, Mistral, DeepSeek.

items.name: Local AI starter model (llama3.2:1b, ~1.3 GB)
items.desc: The small model the Command Center copilot uses by default. Runs on CPU, answers in seconds on a laptop, and is enough for health briefs, checklists and log triage without leaving the machine.

items.name: Pull starter models (coder, chat, reasoning, embeddings, vision)
items.desc: qwen2.5-coder for code, llama3.2 for chat, deepseek-r1 for reasoning, nomic-embed-text for embeddings and llava for vision. Roughly 12 GB.

items.name: LM Studio
items.desc: GUI for running and serving local models (the closest thing to a 'Qwen Studio').

items.name: MCP runtime prerequisites
items.desc: uvx and npx must be on PATH for MCP servers to launch.

items.name: MCP servers (filesystem, memory, git, fetch, time, playwright, context7, firebase, desktop-commander)
items.desc: Pre-caches the reference MCP servers so Claude Desktop launches them instantly.

items.name: Write claude_desktop_config.json
items.desc: Merges the installed MCP servers into Claude Desktop's config. Existing entries are preserved; a .bak is written first.

items.name: Write MCP config for Kiro, Cursor, Windsurf and Claude Code
items.desc: Merges the same MCP server set into each IDE's own config - ~/.kiro/settings/mcp.json, ~/.cursor/mcp.json, ~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json and the user scope of ~/.claude.json. Existing entries are kept; a .bak is written first. Nothing is signed in.

items.name: Azure CLI, AWS CLI, Google Cloud CLI
items.desc: The three cloud command lines.

items.name: Google ADK (Agent Development Kit)
items.desc: Python agent framework: pip install google-adk.

items.name: AI SDKs (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google GenAI)
items.desc: Python and Node SDKs for the major model providers.

steps.cmd: py -3 -m pip install --user anthropic openai google-genai mcp
steps.macCmd: python3 -m pip install --user anthropic openai google-genai mcp --break-system-packages

items.name: Windows SDK
items.desc: Headers, libs and tools for native Windows development.

items.name: CLI toolbelt (jq, ripgrep, fzf, curl, wget, fd, bat, delta)
items.desc: The utilities every other script assumes you have.

items.name: Build libraries (OpenSSL, pkg-config, libffi, protobuf)
items.desc: Native dependencies most language ecosystems link against.

items.name: Cascadia Code + JetBrains Mono Nerd Font
items.desc: Terminal fonts with the glyphs Oh My Posh and Starship expect.

steps.cmd: sh -c 'set -e; d=$HOME/.local/share/fonts; mkdir -p $d; for f in CascadiaCode JetBrainsMono; do curl -fsSL -o /tmp/$f.tar.xz https://github.com/ryanoasis/nerd-fonts/releases/latest/download/$f.tar.xz && tar -xJf /tmp/$f.tar.xz -C $d; done; fc-cache -f'

items.name: WSL 2 + Ubuntu 24.04
items.desc: Windows Subsystem for Linux with Ubuntu 24.04 LTS as the default distro. Updates the WSL kernel, pins version 2 and enables systemd. Needs a reboot before the distro can start.

steps.cmd: $cfg = Join-Path $HOME '.wslconfig'; if (-not (Test-Path $cfg)) { Set-Content -Path $cfg -Value "[wsl2]`nmemory=50%`nswap=4GB`nnetworkingMode=mirrored`n" -Encoding ASCII; Write-Output 'wrote .wslconfig' } else { Write-Output '.wslconfig already present - left as is' }

items.name: WSL: dev toolchain inside Ubuntu
items.desc: Inside the Ubuntu distro: build-essential, git, curl, python3 + venv + pip, Node.js LTS (NodeSource), Docker CLI, OpenSSH, and systemd turned on. Runs only after WSL has rebooted once; re-run this item if Ubuntu is not registered yet.

steps.cmd: $d = (wsl -l -q 2>$null | ForEach-Object { $_.Trim() } | Where-Object { $_ -match '^Ubuntu' } | Select-Object -First 1); if (-not $d) { Write-Output 'no Ubuntu distro registered yet - reboot, then re-run this item'; exit 2 }; Write-Output "using $d"

$d = (wsl -l -q 2>$null | ForEach-Object { $_.Trim() } | Where-Object { $_ -match '^Ubuntu' } | Select-Object -First 1); if ($d) { wsl -d $d -u root -- bash -lc 'printf "[boot]\nsystemd=true\n" > /etc/wsl.conf; apt-get update && DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y build-essential git curl wget unzip ca-certificates gnupg python3 python3-pip python3-venv pkg-config libssl-dev openssh-client jq ripgrep fzf htop' }

$d = (wsl -l -q 2>$null | ForEach-Object { $_.Trim() } | Where-Object { $_ -match '^Ubuntu' } | Select-Object -First 1); if ($d) { wsl -d $d -u root -- bash -lc 'curl -fsSL https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_lts.x | bash - && apt-get install -y nodejs' }

$d = (wsl -l -q 2>$null | ForEach-Object { $_.Trim() } | Where-Object { $_ -match '^Ubuntu' } | Select-Object -First 1); if ($d) { wsl -d $d -u root -- bash -lc 'apt-get install -y docker.io docker-compose-v2 && usermod -aG docker $(logname 2>/dev/null || echo ubuntu)' }

items.name: WSL: Debian + Kali (extra distros)
items.desc: Debian and Kali Linux registered beside Ubuntu. Pick this if you want a clean Debian or a pen-testing distro inside Windows.

items.name: archify (Ionity fork)
items.desc: Clones github.com/Ionity-Global-Pty-Ltd/archify (MIT upstream tt-a1i/archify) into the dev root, installs its Node dependencies, and registers it as a global agent skill for Claude Code / Codex / Cursor.

steps.winCmd: $r = if ($env:PROGRAMERLY_DEV_ROOT) { $env:PROGRAMERLY_DEV_ROOT } else { Join-Path $HOME Development }; Set-Location (Join-Path $r "archify\archify"); npm install --no-fund --no-audit

items.name: Ionity brand assets
items.desc: Clones github.com/AntwerpDesignsIonity/ionity-assets1 for logos, icons and Policy 986 AED documents.

items.name: Create Ionity dev workspace
items.desc: Creates the standard folder tree and drops a Policy 986 AED README at the dev root.

items.name: Cursor
items.desc: AI-native fork of VS Code.

items.name: Kiro (AWS agentic IDE)
items.desc: Amazon's agentic IDE - specs, steering files and hooks on a VS Code base. winget on Windows, Homebrew cask on macOS, the signed .deb or tarball on Linux. Sign in yourself on first launch; ProGramerly links nothing.

steps.cmd: sh -c 'set -e; arch=$(uname -m); case $arch in x86_64) a=x64;; aarch64|arm64) a=arm64;; *) echo "unsupported arch $arch"; exit 3;; esac; ver=$(curl -fsSL https://kiro.dev/downloads/ | grep -oE "kiro-ide-[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+-stable-linux-$a\.deb" | head -1 | sed -E "s/kiro-ide-([0-9.]+)-stable.*/\1/"); [ -n "$ver" ] || ver=1.2.4; base=https://prod.download.desktop.kiro.dev/releases/stable/linux-$a/signed/$ver; if command -v apt-get >/dev/null; then curl -fsSL -o /tmp/kiro.deb $base/deb/kiro-ide-$ver-stable-linux-$a.deb && sudo apt-get install -y /tmp/kiro.deb; else mkdir -p $HOME/.local/opt && curl -fsSL $base/tar/kiro-ide-$ver-stable-linux-$a.tar.gz | tar -xz -C $HOME/.local/opt && ln -sf $HOME/.local/opt/Kiro*/kiro $HOME/.local/bin/kiro 2>/dev/null || true; fi'

items.name: Windsurf
items.desc: Codeium's agentic editor.

pre.cmd: sh -c 'if command -v apt-get >/dev/null; then curl -fsSL https://windsurf-stable.codeiumdata.com/wVxQEIWkwPUEAGf3/windsurf.gpg | gpg --dearmor | sudo tee /usr/share/keyrings/windsurf-stable-archive-keyring.gpg >/dev/null && echo "deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/windsurf-stable-archive-keyring.gpg arch=amd64] https://windsurf-stable.codeiumdata.com/wVxQEIWkwPUEAGf3/apt stable main" | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/windsurf.list >/dev/null && sudo apt-get update; fi'

items.name: Zed
items.desc: Rust-built editor, very fast, good multiplayer.

items.name: JetBrains Toolbox
items.desc: One launcher that installs and updates every JetBrains IDE. Tick the individual IDEs below if you want them installed outright.

steps.cmd: sh -c 'set -e; url=$(curl -fsSL "https://data.services.jetbrains.com/products/releases?code=TBA&latest=true&type=release" | python3 -c "import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)[\"TBA\"][0][\"downloads\"][\"linux\"][\"link\"])"); mkdir -p $HOME/.local/share/JetBrains && curl -fsSL "$url" | tar -xz -C $HOME/.local/share/JetBrains && "$(ls -d $HOME/.local/share/JetBrains/jetbrains-toolbox-*/ | tail -1)jetbrains-toolbox" >/dev/null 2>&1 &'

items.name: IntelliJ IDEA Community
items.desc: Java and Kotlin IDE, the free Community edition.

items.name: PyCharm Community
items.desc: Python IDE, the free Community edition. Pairs with the managed venv.

items.name: WebStorm
items.desc: JavaScript and TypeScript IDE. Free for non-commercial use.

items.name: JetBrains Rider
items.desc: .NET and Unity IDE. Free for non-commercial use.

items.name: CLion
items.desc: C and C++ IDE with CMake and embedded (OpenOCD, ST-Link, PlatformIO) support. Free for non-commercial use.

items.name: Eclipse IDE (Java + C/C++)
items.desc: Eclipse IDE for Java Developers and Eclipse IDE for C/C++ Developers (CDT - the base many vendor IDEs such as STM32CubeIDE build on).

items.name: Sublime Text 4
items.desc: Fast native text editor. Evaluation licence until you buy one.

items.name: Notepad++
items.desc: The Windows quick editor. Opens anything, instantly.

items.name: Helix + Lapce
items.desc: Two Rust-built editors: Helix in the terminal (modal, tree-sitter, LSP built in) and Lapce on the desktop.

items.name: Neovim
items.desc: Modal editor for the terminal.

items.name: Unity Hub
items.desc: Installs the Hub; pick editor versions inside it. Sign in there, not here.

pre.cmd: sh -c 'if command -v apt-get >/dev/null; then wget -qO- https://hub.unity3d.com/linux/keys/public | gpg --dearmor | sudo tee /usr/share/keyrings/Unity_Technologies_ApS.gpg >/dev/null && echo "deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/Unity_Technologies_ApS.gpg] https://hub.unity3d.com/linux/repos/deb stable main" | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/unityhub.list >/dev/null && sudo apt-get update; fi'

items.name: Godot Engine
items.desc: Open-source 2D/3D engine, standard build.

items.name: Edge Dev + Firefox Developer Edition
items.desc: The other two engines, so a site can be tested where it actually breaks.

items.name: Chrome extensions (uBlock Origin Lite + Claude)
items.desc: Ad and tracker blocking plus Claude in Chrome. On Windows with administrator rights both are added to Chrome's force-install policy list; otherwise the Web Store pages open so you can add them with one click.

items.name: WhatsApp Desktop
items.desc: The desktop client. Link your phone yourself afterwards - ProGramerly never touches an account.

items.name: Microsoft Teams
items.desc: The new Teams client.

items.name: Zoom
items.desc: Meetings client.

items.name: Slack + Discord
items.desc: Team chat and community chat.

items.name: Telegram + Signal
items.desc: Two more messengers, both desktop clients.

items.name: Google Drive for desktop
items.desc: Streams or mirrors My Drive and shared drives as a local drive letter. Sign in yourself afterwards.

items.name: Microsoft OneDrive
items.desc: Usually already on Windows - this item makes sure it is current. Sign in yourself afterwards.

items.name: Dropbox
items.desc: The desktop sync client.

items.name: rclone
items.desc: One CLI for every cloud - Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, S3, B2 - sync, mount, copy. Run `rclone config` to add remotes yourself.

items.name: OpenCode
items.desc: Terminal coding agent, provider agnostic.

items.name: Aider
items.desc: Pair programming in the terminal against your git history.

items.name: More agent CLIs (Cline, Goose, Continue, Aichat)
items.desc: A second bench of terminal agents so you are never stuck on one vendor.

items.name: Managed Python environment (.venvs/ionity)
items.desc: One virtual environment every AI and data item below installs into, at Development/.venvs/ionity. Nothing lands in the system Python.

items.name: PyTorch (torch, torchvision, torchaudio)
items.desc: CPU wheels by default - they work on every machine. Swap in a CUDA or ROCm index later if you have the hardware.

items.name: Hugging Face stack (transformers, datasets, accelerate)
items.desc: transformers, datasets, accelerate, tokenizers, safetensors, sentence-transformers and the huggingface CLI.

items.name: TensorFlow + Keras
items.desc: TensorFlow with Keras 3 and TensorBoard.

items.name: Data science toolkit (numpy, pandas, sklearn, Jupyter)
items.desc: numpy, pandas, scipy, scikit-learn, matplotlib, seaborn, JupyterLab, ipykernel, OpenCV, Pillow.

items.name: Agent frameworks (LangChain, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, CrewAI)
items.desc: The orchestration layer plus the Anthropic, OpenAI and Google SDKs, inside the managed venv.

items.name: SQLite + DB Browser
items.desc: The engine, the CLI and a GUI that opens a .db file without ceremony.

items.name: MongoDB Community + Compass + mongosh
items.desc: Server, shell, database tools and the Compass GUI.

items.name: PostgreSQL + pgAdmin
items.desc: PostgreSQL server, client tools and the pgAdmin console.

items.name: MySQL + Workbench
items.desc: MySQL Community Server and MySQL Workbench.

items.name: SQL Server Express + SSMS + Azure Data Studio
items.desc: Microsoft's stack: the Express engine, Management Studio and Azure Data Studio.

items.name: Redis + DBeaver universal client
items.desc: DBeaver talks to every engine above. Redis runs natively on macOS; on Windows it lives in WSL or Docker, and RedisInsight is the console for it.

items.name: XAMPP (Apache + MariaDB + PHP + Perl)
items.desc: The classic local LAMP stack in one installer.

items.name: PHP + Composer + Laravel + Symfony
items.desc: PHP CLI, Composer, the Laravel installer and the Symfony CLI.

items.name: Ruby on Rails
items.desc: Rails, Bundler and the Rails command line, on top of the Ruby runtime.

items.name: Django + DRF + PostgreSQL/MySQL drivers
items.desc: Django, Django REST Framework, Celery, Gunicorn and the drivers for both PostgreSQL and MySQL, in the managed venv.

items.name: React, Express, Vite, Nest, PM2
items.desc: The JavaScript side: Vite and create-vite for React, the Express generator, NestJS CLI, nodemon, PM2, serve and concurrently.

items.name: MERN starter project
items.desc: Writes a working React + Express + MongoDB starter into Development/Sandbox/mern-starter - server, client, scripts and a README - ready to npm install and run.

items.name: .NET web tooling (EF Core, ASP.NET, Azure Functions)
items.desc: dotnet-ef, the ASP.NET scaffolder, the user-secrets tool and the Azure Functions Core Tools.

items.name: Flutter + Dart SDK
items.desc: The Flutter SDK and the Dart toolchain.

items.name: Kotlin + Gradle + Maven
items.desc: The Kotlin compiler and the two JVM build systems everything Android leans on.

items.name: Android SDK command line tools + platform tools
items.desc: sdkmanager, adb and fastboot without opening Android Studio, plus a licence acceptance pass.

steps.winCmd: if (Get-Command sdkmanager -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) { cmd /c "echo y| sdkmanager --licenses" }

items.name: React Native + Expo
items.desc: The Expo tooling, EAS CLI and the React Native community CLI.

items.name: Arduino IDE 2 + arduino-cli + cores
items.desc: Arduino IDE 2 and the arduino-cli it is built on, then the board cores: AVR (Uno/Nano/Mega), SAMD, Mbed RP2040 (Pico), ESP32 (Espressif), ESP8266 and the community RP2040 core. Linux also adds you to the dialout group so the serial port works without sudo.

steps.cmd: arduino-cli lib install "Adafruit NeoPixel" "Adafruit Unified Sensor" "DHT sensor library" ArduinoJson PubSubClient WiFiManager "Adafruit SSD1306" "Adafruit GFX Library" "OneWire" "DallasTemperature" "Servo" "LiquidCrystal I2C" "ESP32Servo"
sudo usermod -aG dialout,uucp $USER 2>/dev/null || sudo usermod -aG dialout $USER

items.name: PlatformIO Core + IDE extension
items.desc: PlatformIO in the managed venv, the VS Code extension, and udev/driver setup where it applies. This is the best embedded IDE going.

post.cmd: sh -c 'curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/platformio/platformio-core/develop/platformio/assets/system/99-platformio-udev.rules | sudo tee /etc/udev/rules.d/99-platformio-udev.rules >/dev/null && sudo udevadm control --reload-rules && sudo udevadm trigger && sudo usermod -aG dialout,plugdev $USER'

items.name: ESP-IDF tooling, esptool, MicroPython, Thonny
items.desc: esptool, mpremote, adafruit-ampy and the Thonny editor, plus the ESP-IDF VS Code extension.

items.name: ESP-IDF v5 (Espressif IoT Development Framework)
items.desc: A shallow clone of the current ESP-IDF v5 release into <dev root>/Hardware/esp-idf, then Espressif's own install script for the esp32, esp32s3, esp32c3, esp32c6 and esp32h2 targets. Activate with `export.ps1` / `export.sh`. ~3 GB.

items.name: VS Code embedded extension set
items.desc: Arduino (community), PlatformIO, ESP-IDF, Cortex-Debug, Serial Monitor, Wokwi simulator, C/C++ tools, CMake, MicroPython (Pymakr) and the Raspberry Pi Pico extension - installed with --force so a re-run repairs them.

items.name: Serial terminals & flashing tools
items.desc: PuTTY and Tera Term 5 on Windows; minicom, picocom and screen on macOS and Linux. Plus esptool, pyserial and the serial-port permissions so a board shows up the moment it is plugged in.

post.cmd: sudo usermod -aG dialout,uucp $USER 2>/dev/null || sudo usermod -aG dialout $USER

items.name: Raspberry Pi Imager + balenaEtcher
items.desc: Write Raspberry Pi OS, Ubuntu or any image to an SD card or USB stick. Pi Imager for Pi boards, Etcher for everything else.

items.name: STM32 & ARM Cortex tooling (OpenOCD, GNU Arm toolchain, stlink)
items.desc: The open toolchain for STM32 and other Cortex-M parts: arm-none-eabi-gcc, OpenOCD and the stlink tools. STM32CubeIDE itself needs an ST account to download, so it is left to you - CLion or VS Code + Cortex-Debug drive this toolchain directly.

post.cmd: if (Get-Command choco -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) { choco install openocd stlink -y --no-progress --limit-output } else { Write-Output 'Chocolatey not present - OpenOCD/stlink skipped; pyocd (serial-tools) covers Cortex-M flashing' }

items.name: Blender
items.desc: 3D modelling, rendering, animation.

items.name: FreeCAD
items.desc: Parametric CAD - parts, assemblies, drawings, CAM path.

items.name: KiCad
items.desc: Schematic capture and PCB layout, with the symbol and footprint libraries.

items.name: PrusaSlicer + Cura
items.desc: Two slicers for 3D printing.

items.name: Processing 4
items.desc: The sketchbook for visual art and interactive installations - the environment Arduino's IDE grew out of. Java under the hood.

items.name: Postman + Insomnia
items.desc: Two API consoles - Postman for collections and teams, Insomnia when you want something lighter.

items.name: HTTPie, Newman, OpenAPI tooling
items.desc: Newman for Postman collections in CI, Redocly and swagger tooling for specs, HTTPie for one-liners.

items.name: Bruno
items.desc: Offline-first API client; collections live in git as plain files.

items.name: Twilio CLI
items.desc: twilio-cli for SMS, WhatsApp Business, Verify and Voice from the terminal. Log in later with `twilio login`.

items.name: Firebase CLI + local emulators
items.desc: firebase-tools, then the Firestore, Database, Storage, Pub/Sub and Emulator UI jars so `firebase emulators:start` works offline. Needs Java. Nothing is deployed and no project is linked.

items.name: Serverless CLIs (AWS SAM, Azure Functions, Wrangler, Vercel, Netlify)
items.desc: AWS Lambda through SAM, Azure Functions Core Tools, Cloudflare Workers via Wrangler, plus Vercel and Netlify. Firebase has its own item.

items.name: Cloudflare WARP + cloudflared
items.desc: The Cloudflare desktop client and the tunnel daemon.

items.name: n8n (workflow automation, self-hosted)
items.desc: npm install -g n8n, then `n8n` opens the editor on http://localhost:5678. Runs on this machine only.

items.name: OpenRGB
items.desc: Vendor-neutral RGB control: motherboard 12V and 5V ARGB headers, GPU, RAM, AIO, fans. ProGramerly's Hardware tab talks to its SDK server.

items.name: FanControl
items.desc: Fan curves for every header, GPU and pump. Ships the signed kernel driver that makes writing to the EC possible.

items.name: LibreHardwareMonitor
items.desc: Temperatures, fan RPM, voltages and power straight off the chips. The sensor source for ProGramerly's Hardware tab.

items.name: curl
items.desc: The transfer tool every install script assumes. Windows ships an older curl.exe; this puts the current one on PATH. Homebrew curl on macOS.

items.name: Google Antigravity IDE
items.desc: Google's agent-first IDE - agents across workspaces, VS Code-familiar editing. winget Google.AntigravityIDE; Homebrew cask antigravity.

items.name: Google Antigravity CLI (agy)
items.desc: The Antigravity agent harness in the terminal. Installed with Google's own script: curl -fsSL https://antigravity.google/cli/install.cmd, run, delete. Binary is `agy`; run it once to sign in.

items.name: Antigravity auto-accept (Ionity)
items.desc: Clones github.com/Ionity-Global-Pty-Ltd/antigravity-auto-accept into your dev root - Ionity's utility that accepts Antigravity agent steps without a click each time.

items.name: Gemma family (gemma4:e2b + gemma3:1b)
items.desc: Google's Gemma on this machine. gemma4:e2b is the everyday model - strong instruction following, reads long context, and still answers on a laptop; gemma3:1b is the pocket version for quick triage. Both run through the same local Ollama the Command Center uses, so nothing leaves the machine.

items.name: Gemma, the larger cut (gemma4:e4b, gemma3:4b)
items.desc: The bigger Gemma weights for a workstation with the memory to hold them: gemma4:e4b for long reasoning and document work, gemma3:4b as the middle step. Roughly 13 GB together.

items.name: Tiny OCR and vision (moondream + granite3.2-vision)
items.desc: Reading models small enough to run beside everything else. moondream is about 1.7 GB and describes and transcribes a screenshot in seconds; granite3.2-vision is built for documents - tables, forms, invoices and scanned pages. Both answer through the local Ollama, so a document never leaves the machine to be read.

items.name: Tesseract OCR engine
items.desc: The classic OCR engine, on PATH. Fast, deterministic, no model to load - the right tool for clean scans and screenshots, and the fallback when no vision model is pulled.

steps.cmd: sh -c 'if command -v apt-get >/dev/null; then sudo apt-get install -y tesseract-ocr; elif command -v dnf >/dev/null; then sudo dnf install -y tesseract; elif command -v pacman >/dev/null; then sudo pacman -S --noconfirm tesseract; else echo "no supported package manager"; exit 1; fi'

items.name: OCR toolkit (RapidOCR, EasyOCR, PyMuPDF)
items.desc: The document-reading stack in the managed Python environment: rapidocr-onnxruntime (tiny, CPU, no system dependency), easyocr for harder pages, pytesseract to drive the engine above, PyMuPDF and pdf2image to turn PDF pages into images, and Pillow for the rest.
